claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC solid solution.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1719 MPa.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has limited room-temperature compressive plasticity.
Changing the composition from equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo to Nb1.2ZrTiHfMo0.8 will maintain high compressive yield strength while significantly increasing plasticity.
Lowering Mo and increasing Nb will reduce the local electronegativity difference.
Lowering Mo and increasing Nb will diminish lattice distortion.
High Mo content produces a large electronegativity difference in NbZrTiHfMo.
Mo contributes to solid-solution strengthening and higher room-temperature strength.
The electronegativity mismatch associated with high Mo content pins dislocations.
High Mo content restricts activation of additional slip systems.
Replacing part of the Mo with Nb will facilitate dislocation mobility and activate additional slip systems.
The modified alloy will retain sufficient solid-solution strengthening to avoid a significant loss of compressive yield strength.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1600–1700 MPa.
The modified alloy will show a 30–50% increase in room-temperature compressive plastic strain before failure.
The beneficial effect is limited to a composition range in which partial Mo-to-Nb substitution does not trigger detrimental phase changes.
Excessive reduction of Mo may cause a significant loss of yield strength.
The alloy series will be tested under identical processing conditions by room-temperature uniaxial compression, XRD, and SEM.
A yield-strength loss greater than about 10% or a plastic-strain improvement below 30% is specified as a falsifying observation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis concerns an optimized composition and explicitly allows ineffective compositions outside a beneficial range, but the falsification rule says failure of any single reduced-Mo composition falsifies the hypothesis. One poorly chosen substitution ratio cannot falsify the existence of an optimum elsewhere in the stated range.
